extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Allergic rhinitis
extraction.clinical_plan: Stop Allegra. Try Zyrtec or loratadine. Use Nasonex samples and prescription (two sprays in each nostril for three weeks).
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: The patient was diagnosed with allergic rhinitis (hay fever). It was recommended to change the current antihistamine medications as they are no longer effective, and a new nasal spray was prescribed.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Discontinue Allegra.
Start taking Zyrtec or a cheaper alternative (Loratadine).
Use Nasonex nasal spray: two sprays into each nostril for 3 weeks.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Left undescended testis plus left inguinal hernia
physical_findings: Type III epididymal attachment with a long looping vas
extraction.clinical_plan: Recovery after left inguinal hernia repair and left orchiopexy.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: Surgical procedure involving the repair of a left inguinal hernia and bringing an undescended left testicle down into the scrotum (orchiopexy).
patient_instructions_target_lang: Rest after the surgical procedure.
Take care of the surgical wounds, which have been secured with a special tissue adhesive (Dermabond).
Follow the pain management instructions provided at discharge.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Mild-to-moderate diverticulosis
medical_history: Cesarean section twice in the past
physical_findings: Few diverticula encountered in the sigmoid and descending colon
extraction.clinical_plan: Patient provided information on diverticulosis including dietary advice. Advised repeat colonoscopy after 10 years.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: A screening colonoscopy was performed. No polyps or neoplastic changes were detected. Only mild to moderate diverticulosis of the colon was noted.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Follow the provided dietary recommendations regarding diverticulosis.
Return for another screening colonoscopy in 10 years.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Left-sided hydronephrosis, ureteral stricture
physical_findings: Properly positioned double-J right ureteral stent
Right kidney measuring 9.0 x 2.9 x 4.3 cm with normal cortical echogenicity
No visible renal or ureteral calculi
extraction.clinical_plan: Review findings with the referring physician for further management of left-sided hydronephrosis.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: An abdominal X-ray and renal ultrasound were performed. The right kidney appears normal, and the indwelling stent is in the correct position. Moderate to severe hydronephrosis was noted in the left kidney. No kidney stones were visualized.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Consult these imaging results with your primary care physician (or urologist) to determine further management for the left hydronephrosis.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Unspecified pain (Indication for caudal epidural steroid injection)
extraction.clinical_plan: Caudal epidural steroid injection with contrast under fluoroscopy guidance.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: An epidural steroid injection procedure (central block) was initiated under X-ray guidance (fluoroscopy). An intravenous line was established, and the patient was given sedative medications (sedation).
patient_instructions_target_lang: Follow the postoperative and anesthesia instructions provided by the medical staff upon waking from sedation.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: 40 weeks 6 days intrauterine pregnancy, non-reassuring fetal heart tones, third-degree midline laceration
medical_history: Positive serology for HSV (no active lesions)
physical_findings: Live male infant with Apgars of 9 and 9
Placenta delivered spontaneously intact with a three-vessel cord
Fetal heart tones dropped to 80s during pushing
extraction.clinical_plan: Patient and baby recovering in LDR in stable condition. Baby will transfer to newborn nursery when ready. Routine postpartum and laceration care.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: A vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery was performed due to a drop in fetal heart rate. A healthy baby boy was delivered. Following the delivery, a third-degree perineal tear and a right vaginal wall laceration were repaired under local anesthesia.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Rest and remain under the care of the staff in the postpartum recovery room.
Maintain meticulous hygiene of your intimate areas due to the stitches placed on the perineum and vaginal wall.
Report any sudden, severe pain or heavy bleeding to a nurse or doctor.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Right renal mass
physical_findings: Early branching of the right renal artery
Minimal degree of oozing from the adrenal gland
extraction.clinical_plan: Recovery after right radical nephrectomy and assisted laparoscopic approach.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: A radical right nephrectomy (kidney removal) was performed due to a tumor. The procedure was completed under general anesthesia using a hand-assisted laparoscopic approach. The surgery was successful without complications.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Rest and follow the routine postoperative instructions provided by the ward staff.
Report any increasing pain at the surgical site to the nurses.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Biliary colic
physical_findings: No injury from entry during laparoscopic examination
extraction.clinical_plan: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: The patient underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy (gallbladder removal) due to biliary colic. No internal injuries were noted during the insertion of surgical instruments.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Rest after your laparoscopic procedure.
Follow the instructions provided by the medical staff upon waking up.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Type I diabetes, recent Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)
physical_findings: Recent blood sugar spike up to >600 mg/dl
extraction.clinical_plan: Dietary consultation for carbohydrate counting. Recommended 1 unit of insulin per 10g carbohydrates and a correction dose of 1 unit per 30 mg/dl drop. Recommended consistent carb intake: 45g breakfast, 45g lunch, 60g dinner. Provided educational materials.

current_medications.name: Humalog / Insulin
current_medications.dosage: Basal: 30.5 units/24 hrs. Boluses: 5 units breakfast, 6 units lunch, 11 units supper. Ratio: 1 unit per 10g carbs. Correction: 1 unit per 30 mg/dl.

extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: Odbyto konsultację dietetyczną dla pacjentki z cukrzycą typu 1, która była niedawno hospitalizowana z powodu kwasicy ketonowej. Omówiono zasady planowania posiłków, przeliczania węglowodanów na jednostki insuliny oraz stosowania dawek korekcyjnych.

A dietary consultation was held for a patient with type 1 diabetes recently hospitalized for diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). Principles of meal planning, carbohydrate-to-insulin ratios, and correction doses were discussed.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Administer 1 unit of insulin for every 10 grams of carbohydrates consumed.
Use a correction dose: 1 unit of insulin lowers blood sugar by approximately 30 mg/dL.
Maintain a consistent carbohydrate intake at meals: 45 g for breakfast, 45 g for lunch, and 60 g for dinner.
In case of any issues with the proper functioning of the insulin pump, call the provided manufacturer's helpline.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Congestive heart failure exacerbation, pneumonia
physical_findings: Decreased air entry in the basilar areas bilaterally
EKG: sinus bradycardia, intraventricular conduction defect, nonspecific ST-T changes
Ejection fraction of 39% with inferior reversible defect (recent scan)
extraction.clinical_plan: Patient admitted to the hospital for further evaluation of congestive heart failure and incidental pneumonia.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: A 75-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital due to shortness of breath, profound fatigue, and right-sided chest and abdominal pain. Tests revealed an exacerbation of congestive heart failure and pneumonia.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Remain in the hospital for further diagnostics and treatment of shortness of breath, heart failure, and pneumonia.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Acute allergic reaction (suspicious for Keflex), Renal failure requiring dialysis, Hypertension
physical_findings: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheeze
Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur
No oropharyngeal masses or lesions, no postnasal drip
extraction.clinical_plan: RAST allergy testing for food and environmental allergies performed. Discontinue cephalosporin antibiotics. Prescribed EpiPen for emergency use.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: An allergy consultation was held following a recent episode of acute swelling, likely triggered by the antibiotic Keflex. RAST allergy testing was performed. Due to the risk of anaphylaxis and the concurrent use of blood pressure medication (Atenolol), an EpiPen auto-injector was prescribed.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Strictly avoid the use of cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., Keflex).
Always carry your EpiPen auto-injector with you.
In the event of sudden swelling, shortness of breath, or a feeling of an impending allergic reaction, use the EpiPen and go immediately to the Emergency Department (ER).

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Obesity (Consultation for laparoscopic gastric bypass)
medical_history: Muscle and joint pains (knee, back, foot, ankle)
Reconstructive surgery on right hand (13 years ago)
extraction.clinical_plan: Evaluation for laparoscopic gastric bypass program. Discussed target weight loss goals (losing 60% of excess body weight to reach approximately 228 lbs).
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: A bariatric consultation was held to qualify the patient for a laparoscopic gastric bypass. Previous complaints (including joint pain, snoring, and reflux) were discussed, and weight reduction goals were established. The patient currently weighs 312 pounds (approx. 141 kg).
patient_instructions_target_lang: Continue attending support group meetings.
Try to completely quit smoking before the planned surgical procedure.
Follow the bariatric program guidelines to prepare your body for surgery.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Right undescended testicle
physical_findings: Testis identified at the external inguinal ring preoperatively
Testicle viable, but smaller than the contralateral side by approximately 50%
extraction.clinical_plan: Right orchiopexy and right herniorrhaphy performed. Patient to follow up in about 1 month.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: A 10-year-old boy underwent surgery to bring down and fixate the right undescended testicle into the scrotum (orchiopexy) and simultaneously repair a small inguinal hernia. The testicle was found to be viable, although slightly smaller than the other one. The procedure went without complications.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Come in for a follow-up appointment in about 1 month.
Do not lift any heavy objects for at least 3 months.
You may take a shower 48 hours after the procedure.
Avoid taking tub baths for the next 2 months.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Perianal abscess, normal colonoscopy to the terminal ileum
physical_findings: Normal mucosa throughout the colon and terminal ileum (no colitis)
Jagged 8-mm opening at the anorectal junction posteriorly (12 o'clock position)
Purulent material expressed through the opening
No evidence of fistulous connection to the bowel lumen
Small dimpled scar 1 cm from the anal verge in the 11 o'clock position
Dimpled scar about 5 cm from the anal verge on the left buttock's cheek
extraction.clinical_plan: Continue current antibiotics and follow up with Dr. X. Consider surgical drainage if purulent drainage persists.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: A colonoscopy was performed due to rectal bleeding and a suspected abscess. The large intestine and terminal ileum are normal, with no inflammation. An 8-mm opening with purulent discharge was identified at the anorectal junction, indicating a draining perianal abscess. No evidence of a fistula was found.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Continue taking your current antibiotics as directed.
Follow up with Dr. X.
If the purulent drainage persists, surgical drainage may be necessary.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Left lower extremity swelling (No evidence of deep venous thrombosis)
physical_findings: Normal compressibility, augmentation, and color/Doppler flow in the common femoral, superficial femoral, and popliteal veins
Flow demonstrated in the proximal posterior tibial vein
No evidence of deep venous thrombosis (DVT) in the left lower extremity
extraction.clinical_plan: Ultrasound results are negative for DVT. Patient to follow up with the referring provider regarding the etiology of the left leg swelling.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: An ultrasound (Doppler) of the left leg was performed due to swelling to rule out thrombosis. The exam showed normal blood flow in all evaluated vessels. Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) was ruled out.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Consult the test results with your referring doctor to determine another cause for the leg swelling.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Unspecified neck/back pain (Indication for cervical epidural steroid injection)
physical_findings: No cerebrospinal fluid or blood noted upon aspiration (loss of resistance technique)
extraction.clinical_plan: Patient discharged to recovery room in stable condition post-procedure.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: An epidural steroid injection (Depo-Medrol) was performed in the cervical spine. The procedure was done under local anesthesia, without the use of X-ray guidance (fluoroscopy). The procedure was successful and without complications.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Rest and remain under observation by the staff in the recovery room.
Keep the injection site (on the back of the neck/upper back) clean; a bandage with antibiotic ointment was applied.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Well-woman checkup, status post hysterectomy, recent urinary tract infection
medical_history: Fall with head trauma and subsequent headaches
physical_findings: Breasts without masses, tenderness, nipple retraction, or discharge
extraction.clinical_plan: Evaluate UTI therapy adequacy with urinalysis and culture. Recommended screening mammogram, hemoccult x 3, DEXA scan, and fasting labs (chem-12, lipid profile, CBC). Continue current medications. Annual recheck.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: The patient presented for a routine well-woman checkup. Medical history includes a hysterectomy and a recent urinary tract infection. The physical examination revealed no abnormalities. A set of preventive screenings was ordered, including a mammogram, DEXA bone density scan, blood tests, and a urinalysis.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Complete the ordered preventive screenings: mammogram, DEXA bone density scan, stool test for occult blood (Hemoccult x 3), and fasting blood tests.
Provide a urine sample for a urinalysis and culture to ensure the urinary tract infection has been fully resolved.
Continue taking your current medications without changes.
Return for another routine checkup in one year unless any concerning symptoms arise.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Right renal mass (suspected renal cell carcinoma)
medical_history: Positive family history of renal cell carcinoma
physical_findings: Right renal mass located in the lower pole laterally
Intraoperative ultrasound showed the mass to be deeper than initially anticipated
Frozen section biopsies from the base of the resection negative for renal cell carcinoma
Tumor close to the margin, but with 1-2 mm normal parenchyma around it
extraction.clinical_plan: Patient transferred to the postanesthesia care unit for postoperative monitoring following a successful laparoscopic right partial nephrectomy.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: A laparoscopic partial right nephrectomy (tumor resection) was performed. Special medications were used during the surgery to protect the kidney from ischemia. The tumor was removed, and rapid histopathological examination (frozen section) confirmed tumor-free margins. The patient woke up without complications.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Rest and remain under close observation by the staff in the postoperative recovery room.
Report any pain or issues with the drain placed in the lumbar area to the nurse.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Acute cholecystitis
medical_history: Previous abdominal surgery (inferred from old incision)
physical_findings: Large gallstones requiring extraction from the gallbladder before removal
extraction.clinical_plan: Patient transferred to the recovery room in stable condition post laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: The patient underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy (gallbladder removal) due to acute cholecystitis. During the surgery, an enlarged gallbladder, large gallstones, and areas of necrosis were noted. The procedure was successful, and the patient was transferred to the recovery room in stable condition.
patient_instructions_target_lang: Rest and remain under the care of the medical staff in the recovery room.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Poison ivy / Poison oak contact dermatitis
physical_findings: Raised, maculopapular rash in a linear pattern over arms, legs, chest, and back
extraction.clinical_plan: Administer Solu-Medrol 125 mg IM once. Instructed to continue OTC Benadryl or the previously prescribed once-a-day allergy medication.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: A 24-year-old male patient presented with an itchy, maculopapular rash in a linear pattern on his chest, back, and extremities, which occurred after contact with poison ivy while fishing. The patient reported similar reactions in the past. An intramuscular steroid injection was recommended to alleviate the acute inflammation.
patient_instructions_target_lang: You received a one-time intramuscular steroid injection (Solu-Medrol), which will help quickly reduce inflammation and itching.
Continue applying cortisone cream to the affected areas of the skin.
You may continue taking over-the-counter Benadryl OR return to taking the prescription allergy medication (taken once a day) that was prescribed to you during your previous visit.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Chronic adenotonsillitis with adenotonsillar hypertrophy, Upper respiratory tract infection with mild acute laryngitis
physical_findings: Clear nasal drainage, large inferior turbinates
Oropharynx reveals very large, exophytic tonsils (3+/4+)
Mirror examination of the larynx reveals mild edema
Patient is a mouth breather at nighttime
History of loud snoring, throat pain, fever, and intermittent hoarseness with infections
extraction.clinical_plan: Scheduled for adenotonsillectomy at Memorial Medical Center in the coming weeks. Risks, benefits, and alternatives of surgery were discussed with the patient and family.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: A 15-year-old female patient presented for an ENT consultation due to recurrent tonsil infections and snoring. The examination revealed significantly enlarged palatine tonsils and mild laryngeal edema associated with a current upper respiratory tract infection. After discussing treatment options, the patient was scheduled for surgical removal of the tonsils and adenoids (adenotonsillectomy).
patient_instructions_target_lang: Carefully review the provided information regarding the planned tonsil removal surgery (including the risks of bleeding or infection).
Wait for the final surgery date to be scheduled at Memorial Medical Center in the coming weeks.

extraction.primary_diagnosis_technical: Respiratory distress and asthma exacerbation
physical_findings: Peak flows decreased from 100 to 75 over the course of the day
Oxygen saturation low at 91% on room air, 99% with treatment, dropping to 92% with coughing spells
Tight wheezing and retractions heard bilaterally
Chest x-ray reveals bronchial thickening, no definite infiltrate
extraction.clinical_plan: Patient admitted to the hospital under the hospitalist service for continued management of respiratory distress and asthma.
extraction.patient_summary_target_lang: A 5-year-old boy was brought to the Emergency Department (ER) due to an asthma exacerbation, severe cough, and wheezing. The examination revealed low blood oxygen (91% saturation) and significant breathing difficulties. After administering inhaled medications, steroids, and oxygen in the ER, the decision was made to admit the child to the hospital for further treatment.
patient_instructions_target_lang: The child is being admitted to the hospital ward to monitor his breathing and continue asthma treatment.
During the hospital stay, the staff will continue administering oxygen, strong bronchodilators, and steroids.
